The green level of the ambient lighting LED.
The red level of the ambient lighting LED.
The Codec2 bitrate to use. The sample rate is always 8 kHz. Lower bitrates use less bandwidth but reduce audio quality.
Enable Codec2 audio encoding/decoding for voice communication over the mesh.
Fixed PIN for Bluetooth pairing. Used when pairing mode is set to fixed PIN
GPIO pin for rotary encoder A port.
GPIO pin for rotary encoder B port.
GPIO pin for rotary encoder Press port.

Enables the detection sensor module, it needs to be enabled on both the node with the sensor, and any nodes that you want to receive detection sensor text messages or view the detection sensor log and chart.
GPIO pin watched for state changes.
Send ASCII bell with alert message. Useful for triggering external notification on bell.
How often to send the detection sensor state to the mesh, whether or not anything was detected.
Whether or not use INPUT_PULLUP mode for GPIO pin. Only applicable if the board uses pull-up resistors on the pin
GPIO pin for the user button, can be remapped on boards with multiple buttons
GPIO pin for the PWM buzzer
Disables the user button triple-press shortcut.
Treat double tap on supported accelerometers as a user button press.
Controls the blinking LED on the device. For most devices this will control one of the up to 4 LEDS, the charger and GPS LEDs are not controllable.
How often node information is sent. Defaults to 900 seconds.
Rebroadcast any observed message, if it was on our private channel or from another channel with the same lora params.
Same as behavior as ALL but skips packet decoding and simply rebroadcasts them. Only available in Repeater role. Setting this on any other roles will result in ALL behavior.
Only rebroadcasts packets from the core portnums: NodeInfo, Text, Position, Telemetry, and Routing.
Ignores observed messages from foreign meshes like Local Only, but takes it step further by also ignoring messages from nodes not already in the node's known list.
Ignores observed messages from foreign meshes that are open or those which it cannot decrypt. Only rebroadcasts message on the nodes local primary / secondary channels.
Only permitted for SENSOR, TRACKER and TAK_TRACKER roles, this will inhibit all rebroadcasts, not unlike CLIENT_MUTE role.
Used for rooftop nodes to distribute messages more widely from multiple nearby client mute nodes.
App connected or stand alone messaging device.
Device that only broadcasts as needed for stealth or power savings.
Device that does not forward packets from other devices.
Broadcasts location as message to default channel regularly for to assist with device recovery.
Deprecated infrastructure role that creates gaps in the mesh rebroadcast chain. Switch this node to a Router-based role (Router or Router Late).
Infrastructure node on a tower or mountain top only. Not to be used for roofs or mobile nodes. Needs exceptional coverage. Visible in Nodes list.
Infrastructure node that always rebroadcasts packets once but only after all other modes. Visible in Nodes list. Not a good choice for rooftop nodes.
Optimized for ATAK system communication, reduces routine broadcasts.
Enables automatic TAK PLI broadcasts and reduces routine broadcasts.
Broadcasts GPS position packets as priority.
Automatically moves to the next screen page, like a carousel, on this interval.
The compass heading on the screen outside of the circle will always point north.
Indicates how to rotate or invert the compass output for accurate display.
Inverted top bar for 2 Color display
Bold the heading text on the screen.
How long the screen remains on after the user button is pressed or messages are received.
Units shown on the device screen.
Sets the screen clock format to 12-hour.
Wake Screen on tap or motion
Requires that there be an accelerometer on your device.
If enabled, the 'output' Pin will be pulled active high, disabled means active low.
Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a bell
Alert GPIO vibra motor when receiving a bell
Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a message
Alert GPIO vibra motor when receiving a message
GPIO pin driven on notification. Defaults to the board's EXT_NOTIFY_OUT pin.
In GPIO mode, how long to keep the output on.
Enables devices with native I2S audio output to use the RTTTL over speaker like a buzzer. T-Watch S3 and T-Deck for example have this capability.
Use a PWM output (like the RAK Buzzer) for tunes instead of an on/off output. This will ignore the output, output duration and active settings and use the device config buzzer GPIO option instead.
Your node’s operating frequency is calculated based on the region, modem preset, and this field. When 0, the slot is automatically calculated based on the primary channel name.
How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded.
Ignore packets received over LoRa that travelled via MQTT anywhere on their path.
The region where you will be using your radios.
Number of chirps per symbol, as 2 raised to this value.
Enable RX boosted gain mode on SX126X based radios
Allow the LoRa radio to transmit. Turn off while hot-swapping antennas or bench testing.
Radio transmit power. Leave at zero to use the highest level legal for the region, which is what most radios should use.
Use the modem preset settings instead of a manual bandwidth, spread factor and coding rate
How often a map report is published.
I have read and understand the above. I voluntarily consent to the unencrypted transmission of my node data via MQTT.
How often a beacon is broadcast.

Your node will periodically send an unencrypted map report packet to the configured MQTT server, this includes id, short and long name, approximate location, hardware model, role, firmware version, LoRa region, modem preset and primary channel name.
Utilizes the network connection on your phone to connect to MQTT.
TLS is required for the public Meshtastic MQTT server.
Enable neighbor info broadcasting. Periodically sends information about directly-heard neighbors to help visualize mesh topology.
Whether to transmit neighbor info over LoRa in addition to MQTT and PhoneAPI. Not available on channels with default key and name.
How often to broadcast neighbor info.
Enable broadcasting packets via UDP over the local network.
Enabling Ethernet will disable the bluetooth connection to the app.
NTP server address. Defaults to meshtastic.pool.ntp.org
Enabling WiFi will disable the bluetooth connection to the app.
WiFi network name to connect to
RSSI threshold for counting BLE devices.
When enabled the PAX Counter module counts the number of people passing by using WiFi and Bluetooth. Both WiFI and Bluetooth must be disabled for PAX counter to work.
How often we can send a message to the mesh when people are detected.
RSSI threshold for counting WiFi devices.
The minimum change in distance before a smart position broadcast is considered.
The shortest interval between position updates once the minimum distance has been met.
The last known latitude, longitude and altitude are broadcast over the mesh on the position interval, rather than a live GPS fix.
How often to try to get a GPS position.
The longest a node will go without broadcasting a position.
Optional fields to include when assembling position messages
Include an altitude value in position reports, when one is available.
Include the dilution of precision value. PDOP is used by default.
If DOP is set, send separate HDOP and VDOP values instead of PDOP.

Will sleep everything as much as possible, for the tracker and sensor role this will also include the lora radio. Don't use this setting if you want to use your device with the phone apps or are using a device without a user button.
How long after external power is removed before the device powers off. Zero to disable.
Saves a CSV with the range test message details, currently only available on ESP32 devices with a web server.
This device will send out range test messages on the selected interval.
The public key authorized to send admin messages to this node
Output live debug logging over serial, view and export position-redacted device logs over Bluetooth.
Device is managed by a mesh administrator, the user is unable to access any of the device settings.
Prefer authenticated packets, but still accept unsigned traffic from nodes not known to sign.
Authenticate packets when possible, but accept unsigned traffic for maximum compatibility
Accept only packets with a verified signature or successful PKI decryption. Packets from older nodes may be ignored.
Used to create a shared key with a remote device
Generated from your private key and sent out to other nodes on the mesh to allow them to compute a shared secret key
Serial Console over the Stream API.
If set, any packets you send will be echoed back to your device.
The amount of time to wait before we consider your packet as done.
Enables the store and forward module.
Send a heartbeat to advertise the server's presence.
Enable this device as a Store and Forward server. Requires an ESP32 device with PSRAM.
How often air quality metrics are sent over the mesh.
Enable broadcasting device metrics to the mesh network. When disabled, metrics are only sent to connected clients.
How often device metrics are sent over the mesh.
How often environment metrics are sent over the mesh.
How often power metrics are sent over the mesh.
Only answer requestors within this many hops.
Positions from the same node arriving sooner than this are dropped.
The most packets one node may send per window.
The time window packets are counted over.
How many per window before the sender is dropped.
